_doc: THE panel definition. One file, one runner (plasma-panels-apply.sh), one
trigger (plasma-manager's run_all.sh autostart, plus the same binary at HM
activation so a switch applies without a logout).
2026-08-24 — why this file exists. Panels used to be defined in FOUR places
that each owned a different slice and fought each other:
top-panel.nix/.json + bottom-panel.nix/.json -> plasma-manager, which
generated desktop_script_panels.js and ran it from XDG autostart;
systray-items.json + plasma-systray-config.sh -> tray CONTENTS, which
plasma-manager structurally cannot write (they live in the PRIVATE
systemtray containment, not the applet), delivered by a systemd user
unit whose .wants symlink was a regular file on this box, so it never
ran and the trays showed Plasma's compiled-in stock icon set;
plasma-panel-repair.json + plasma-fix-missing-panel-widgets.sh -> a
post-pass re-adding widgets plasmashell DROPPED, because plasma-manager
batches every addWidget() across every panel into ONE evaluateScript
call and plasmashell silently drops the 3rd+ call for the same custom
KPackage plugin id in a single script;
plasma-panel-sync.sh -> a reconciler over all of the above, itself
defeated by plasma-manager's 0_script_reset_lastrun_desktopscripts.sh,
which deletes the very markers it seeds whenever the generated JS moves.
plasma-manager no longer defines any panel (programs.plasma.panels is left
empty, so its desktopScript."panels" — and with it the reset script and the
destructive rebuild — is never generated at all). The runner issues ONE
D-Bus evaluateScript call PER WIDGET, so the batching bug that the whole
repair mechanism existed to paper over cannot fire: no insert_after
anchors, no AppletOrder splicing, no orphan sweep. A full rebuild from this
file is the only thing that ever writes the layout, so anything not listed
here is gone by construction rather than by a compensating delete pass.
Panel order below is creation order, and creation order fixes both
panels()[i] and the [Containments][N] order the tray step matches against.
BOTTOM IS FIRST because that is the order the generated script this
replaces actually emitted (verified against the live
~/.local/share/plasma-manager/data/desktop_script_panels.js, which is the
reverse of the old import order in session-default-config.nix). Do not
reorder without re-checking the tray mapping.
alignment defaults to "center" in the runner, matching what the generated
script set on both panels; a panel can override it here.
Dropped in the merge: bottom-panel.json's pager_names (nothing read it —
the virtual-desktop names come from default-session.json).
_always_hidden_doc: There is deliberately no per-tray 'hidden' list: hiddenItems is computed as
the complement of 'shown', because the systray's default for an id it was
never told about is *shown*. Listing hidden items only hides what we
predicted, which is how my-ai-usage, Xwayland Video Bridge and diskquota
leaked in, and how clipboard-systray (registered by the daemon, declared
nowhere) surfaced in tray 2 among the KDE indicators on 2026-08-21.
always_hidden is for ids that must be hidden in EVERY tray.

_doc: Bottom panel. Left-to-right: kickoff, pager, [spacer], icontasks,
[spacer], two system trays. No clock — two clocks on one screen is
just two clocks.
A panelspacer on EACH side of the launchers: both are expanding, so
they split the leftover width evenly and the launcher row lands
centred. With only the trailing one it was pinned against the pager.
icontasks has no centring setting of its own; panel layout is the
mechanism.
No watchdog widget on this panel by request (2026-08-11) — watchdog
lives on the top panel only.
height=70. The old 64 was a workaround for KDE bug 489307, where
org.kde.plasma.systemmonitor's rendered size came from the ksysguard
sensor face and rounded to near-zero on a short horizontal panel. That
widget is gone; watchdog draws its own text and pies, so the panel is
now sized for how it looks.
launchers are freedesktop desktop-ids in pin order.
TWO trays: one holds OUR daemons and shows them permanently, the other
holds KDE's indicators and lets them auto-hide, so battery and volume
appear when they have something to say while nix-flakes, docker and
my-ai stay one click away. A single tray cannot express both policies —
shownItems/hiddenItems are per-tray. Tray 1's ids are the ones
da__my-konsole's configs/systrays.json publishes (one --tray-daemon
process, NINE items).

widgets._doc: Tray 1 — our own daemons, always visible.

_doc: Top panel. Left-to-right: storage, mem, cpu, network, proctable,
[spacer], clock, [spacer], guard, psi — psi deliberately rightmost.
The eight org.kde.plasma.systemmonitor widgets that used to live here
are gone. Each instance builds a sensor-face controller and a
KQuickCharts scene graph inside plasmashell; fourteen of them settled
at ~24% CPU and 410MB (135MB of it QML JS heap) to show eight numbers,
while ksystemstats — which actually reads /proc — measures 2.5%. The
com.diegonmarcos.watchdog widgets read one JSON my-konsole's tray
daemon publishes every 2s and draw text, so adding a metric costs a
label rather than another sub-application. PSI is displayable at all
only because of that: /proc/pressure has no KSystemStats backend, which
is why the old panel faked it with diskusage widgets pointed at
pressure paths under titles that named something else.
The plasmoid is vendored in this flake (modules/dotfiles/kde/plasmoids/
com.diegonmarcos.watchdog) since 2026-08-22, so it comes from a store
path rather than a working-tree cp.
panelspacer carries no config: the applet's own QML default is
expanding=true, so the two of them centre the clock between the groups.

widgets._doc: The process table. Not a summary duplicate: a sortable per-process table (cpu/mem/rss/psi-cpu/read/write) with the full kill-signal menu. Its compact form is one headline label, so it costs a panel slot the width of a word; the table is the expanded popup. It sits at the end of the left group because 8a285547 took watchdog off the bottom panel entirely.

dateFormat=longDate is the full date WITH weekday under the time. It was live-only drift until 2026-08-21: set by hand in the GUI, present in appletsrc, declared nowhere — and undeclared panel state does not survive a rebuild from this file, which is exactly how it would silently revert to time-only.
